## Target: the host's part of an evaluation of a large frame
These are the profile medians of `fitting_paths` in the large-frame-split record (build a08daf6, held to the
P-cores), for water se_e2_a in float32 with the tables looked up:
| Atoms | host_prepare | issue.neighbors | host_finish | Host total | Median evaluation | Share |
The card idles while the host does this work: nsys shows about 3.2 ms before the first kernel at 98,304 atoms.
The share is about the same at both sizes, so a host-side saving would count at 12,288 atoms too, where PR C's
candidates fell short of 4%. In float64 the host part is about 3 of 250 ms (1.2%), so float64 is only a control.
In the code all of it is single-threaded (`gpu_model.rs` `run`; `gpu/src/nlist.rs` `search` and `pack`):
- **host_prepare:**
- `Frame::type_ids` validates the frame, validates the model's metadata again (`ModelMetadata::validate`: a
`HashSet` and a scan of the element list for every name), and maps every species, one `String` per atom, into a
new `Vec<i32>`;
- the counts by type;
- the sort by type into the kept scratch.
- **issue.neighbors:**
- the results buffer: `cuMemAllocAsync`, which pools, then a clear;
- the search's checks of its input (types in range, positions finite, systems);
- the search's `plan` and `fill`: the counting sort into cells and the packed input;
- the comparison of the types with the last search's;
- the upload of the packed input (5.52 MB at 98,304 atoms);
- the launches.
- **host_finish:**
- a new `vec![[0.0; 3]; natoms]` of forces for every evaluation (2.36 MB at 98,304 atoms). Its pages are fresh
each time, because the caller drops the last evaluation;
- the scatter of the forces into frame order;
- `validate`.
The bench's timed loop drops each pass's evaluations inside the timed interval (`omnimd-native-gpu-eval.rs`, the
loop over `passes`), so the drop counts in the median evaluation. `in_parallel` (one spawned thread per logical
processor, about 1 ms a call by step 0) serves only `tabulate` and `tabulate_pairs` under `compress`, not an
evaluation.
## Step 0 (done 2026-11-26 02:58 to 03:03; i9-14900K; `tools/prd/forkjoin.rs`, `forkjoin2.rs`)
- `std::thread::available_parallelism()` gives 32 under the P-core mask `0xFFFC` (14 processors) as well as
unmasked. So the thread count is taken from the process affinity mask (`GetProcessAffinityMask`), never from
`available_parallelism`.
- Spawning per job is ruled out. `std::thread::scope` with k - 1 spawned threads took a median of 43 µs at k = 2,
173 at k = 7 and 361 at k = 14 (P-cores, jobs back to back). k = 7 alone costs more than the whole budget at
12,288 atoms.
- A pool of k - 1 workers parked between jobs (`thread::park` and `unpark`), timed as an evaluation would use it:
the calling thread spins for a gap (the device's work), then issues 3 dispatches one after the other. Medians of
the sum of the 3, in µs (90th percentile in brackets):
- So (b) needs a parked pool, few dispatches an evaluation, and a small k. A pool's overhead at 12,288 atoms (about
25 to 60 µs for 3 dispatches at k = 4 to 8) leaves room under the host total of 0.371 ms, so a threshold T at or
below 12,288 stays tenable. Whether (b) can carry the 4% bar there depends on how fast the loops run on k
threads, which step 1b measures.
## Step 1: split the three parts (a measurement; nothing of it kept)
- A probe build, never committed, adds host marks inside the three parts, at the boundaries listed above. Inside
`type_ids`, the frame's validation, the model's validation and the mapping are marked apart. The probe also
times the caller's drop of the last evaluation.
- The probe has two modes, chosen by an environment variable:
- **Mode A** is the unchanged path plus the marks.
- **Mode B** emulates (a): each pass writes into evaluations that the bench keeps from the last pass, so no
forces buffer is allocated or dropped.
- Only mode A is held to the base's stage medians (below).
- Cases: water 12,288 and 98,304 atoms in float32 with tables, and 98,304 in float64. 5 rounds: base, probe in
mode A, probe in mode B, base again, alternated in one session. Held to the P-cores (`affine.py 0xFFFC`), with the
card checked free before every round. An earlier host probe (2026-11-22, before #43 merged) is kept in
`tools/prd` for its design only; its numbers predate #43 and #44 and are not used.
- **The probe must not move what it measures.** Mode A's medians of host_prepare, issue.neighbors and host_finish
must each match the base build's within max(spread, 2%), where the spread is that of the base against the base
again in the same rounds. Otherwise the split is not used. A check that the parts add up proves nothing, since
marks partition an interval by construction.
- Each part is reported in ms and as a share of the median evaluation of the same run, with that base named.
## Step 1b, after step 1: the loops of (b) on k threads
- A probe, never committed, holds a prototype of the pool and parallel versions of the loops of (b). It runs on
the real code paths, each loop serial and on 2, 4 and 7 threads, at 1,536, 3,072, 6,144, 12,288 and 98,304
atoms. The 3,072- and 6,144-atom frames are the 1,536-atom water cell replicated twice along one axis and along
two axes. It runs once held to the P-cores and once unmasked, timed with the gap and the dispatches an
evaluation has.
- **Floor:** a loop whose time in step 1 is below 20 µs at 12,288 atoms (median, P-cores) stays serial and projects
zero. The prototype, and any design review of it, covers only the pool and the loops above the floor.
## Step 2: candidates, each with its projected saving
- **(a) Forces into evaluations the caller keeps.**
- The production callers are the engine's calls of `Potential::eval`, `eval_batch` and `Committee::eval_members`
(`mlmd/engine/src/main.rs`, `deviation.rs`, `dataset_commands.rs`). There is no exported C interface (no
`#[no_mangle]` in `mlmd`).
- So (a) is a method of the contract's traits with a default implementation (non-breaking), for example
`eval_into(&mut self, frame, out: &mut Evaluation)`. The engine's MD loop and the bench take it. A call that
only the bench takes would be a gain of the bench alone, and does not count.
- No threshold, no threads, no unsafe code.
- Projected saving: mode A's host_finish plus its drop, minus mode B's.
- **(d) Serial work repeated in every evaluation, removed without threads.** The list is closed:
1. the model's validation inside `type_ids` (the metadata does not change once the potential is built);
2. the new `Vec<i32>` of types that `type_ids` returns for every frame, replaced by a buffer the potential keeps;
3. the small vectors `run` allocates in every evaluation (counts, block, cursor, cells, pair_rows, works and the
groups of the fitting), together.
- (d) removes no check on a frame or a result. The frame's validation, the search's checks of its input and the
evaluations' `validate` all stay.
- No threshold. Results identical to the bit.
- Projected saving: the step 1 time of each item (median, P-cores). An item below 5 µs at 12,288 atoms, or one
the probe cannot isolate, projects zero.
- **(b) The loops above the floor on a parked pool, in passes of at least T atoms.**
- The pool is std only: k - 1 workers started once and parked between dispatches, the calling thread taking a
share. A dispatch returns, and unwinds, only after every job of it has finished, including when a job or the
caller panics.
- Its unsafe core (borrowed jobs on persistent workers need their lifetimes erased) gets a review of its own.
Miri is not installed (the isolated toolchain is stable only; nightly would be a download the user approves),
so tests cover the panic paths: a job that panics, and a caller that panics while jobs run.
- Each loop keeps its order, so the device sees the same input to the bit.
- **k = min(c, the number of processors in the process affinity mask)**, with c one of 2, 4 and 7, chosen once in
step 1b at 12,288 atoms. c is the value whose total time for the loops above the floor (unmasked, median, with
the dispatches) is least; if two are within 5% of each other, the smaller wins. The same c serves every size.
- **T** is the least of the sizes of step 1b at which, at that size and every larger one, the loops on k threads
(unmasked, median, with the dispatches) take at least 10% less than the serial loops. T is at most 12,288. If
no size up to 12,288 qualifies, (b) projects zero at 12,288 and is confined to the least larger size that
qualifies; 12,288 is then a not-slower control for it.
- T is settable from tests: a getter and setter as with `device_sums_centers`, where `Some(0)` threads every
pass, `Some(usize::MAX)` none, and `None` restores the default.
- Projected saving: for each loop above the floor, its step 1 time minus its step 1b time on k threads with the
dispatches. The unmasked figures serve the not-slower clause.
- **(c) The packing on the device:** positions, types and systems are uploaded, then binned by a kernel.
- Projected saving: plan, fill and the upload's excess bytes, minus the kernel's time at 900 GB/s of its bytes.
**Each saving is counted once across candidates.** They overlap, so a later candidate projects only what the
earlier ones leave:
- (a) and (b) share the scatter of the forces: (b) projects its scatter from mode B's time;
- (d) and (b) share the type mapping: (b) projects it from its time without (d)'s items;
- (b) and (c) share plan and fill: whichever comes second projects only what the first leaves of them.
## Choice (the bars of PR C's rule 1)
- PR D takes (a), then (d), then whichever of (b) and (c) projects the larger saving at 12,288 atoms, then the
other. It stops as soon as the projected savings together reach both bars:
- at least 0.8 ms of the median evaluation at 98,304 atoms;
- at least 4% of the median at 12,288 atoms.
- (b) no longer ranks as cheaper than (c): it carries a pool with unsafe code, (c) a kernel with the sanitizer's
checks.
- If all four together fall short, PR D takes the neighbor search kernel instead, under a rule of its own. That
kernel is 2.69 ms of 20.25 (13%) at 98,304 atoms and 0.36 of 2.61 (14%) at 12,288, by nsys kernel times against
the profile medians.
- (b) and (c) are confined to passes past their threshold, so that the small HAP frames and committees keep their
code and serve as the control.
- Each candidate taken lands as a PR of its own, in the order above. A candidate that projects less than 1% of the
median at both 12,288 and 98,304 atoms does not stand alone: it rides in the next PR taken.
## A/B (written now, before any code)
The A/B has two jobs, judged apart.
**Each PR** against the base build before it (`run/prev-<merge before the change>`):
- The runs: base, the change, base again, 5 rounds alternated. Held to the P-cores, with the card checked free
before every round. The least of each case is kept. One more round runs unmasked, since production is not pinned
and threads will land on the efficiency cores.
- Keep the PR only if all of these hold:
1. It is not slower than the base beyond max(spread, 1%) anywhere: float32 with tables at 12,288 and 98,304
atoms; float64 at 98,304 atoms; the cases of the small set of #44 (HAP frames and committees); and the
unmasked round, at 12,288 and 98,304 atoms.
2. At each of 12,288 and 98,304 atoms (float32 with tables, P-cores) where its own projected saving is more than
1% of the median, it is faster than the base beyond max(spread, 1%).
3. Energies, forces and virials are identical to the base's to the bit, at 88, 12,288 and 98,304 atoms, in
float32 and float64. (a), (d) and (b) reorder no sum, so this is the right bar for them. (c) is held to it as
well, since the order of atoms in each cell must stay the same.
- Rule 3 of PR C stays: anything else slower beyond max(spread, 2%) is looked into.
**The bars**, once, on the cumulative build of every PR of PR D against `run/prev-af9ff5a`, with the same runs:
- at least 0.8 ms less at 98,304 atoms, and at least 4% less at 12,288 atoms (float32 with tables, P-cores,
medians);
- if either bar is missed, the merged PRs stay, since each was kept by its own A/B, and the large-frame plan moves
on to the neighbor search kernel under a rule of its own.
**Checks of each PR:**
- every suite in both profiles;
- for (b), a new suite test that forces the threaded loops on and off and holds the two paths equal to the bit. It
covers a batch and an open cell, since `plan` branches on `system`; the suites' frames are small, so without it
the new path runs only in the manual A/B. Also tests of the pool's panic paths;
- the PTX of all 76 kernels identical to the base's, for (a), (d) and (b) (host-only);
- for (c) only, compute-sanitizer. Racecheck runs with `--racecheck-report hazard`, with a positive control, and
the binary of every run is logged.
## The three lessons of PR C's review, as clauses of this rule
1. **Count each part once.** `issue.neighbors` holds both the packing and the upload. A part named twice is
counted once, within a split and across candidates (step 2). Whether the probe moved the stages is checked
against the base build, as in step 1.
2. **Name every share's base.** Use the median evaluation of the same run held to the P-cores, or an nsys window,
never mixed in one figure.
3. **No host splits from unpinned traces.** Host times come only from runs held to the P-cores, plus the unmasked
rounds named above. nsys is used for device kernels and for whether the card idles; its host-side times are not
quoted.
# PR D rule, amendment 1: the session of step 1
Written 2026-11-26 04:46 (UTC-6), after step 1's first session (`split-1.json`, `split-1.txt`, notes in
`split-1-notes.md`) and the advisor's review of it, before any further run. This file's creation time is the time
of the amendment. It changes how step 1's session is run, and fixes two figures the rule left open. Nothing else in
`rule-pr-d.txt` changes.
## What happened, and why the session changes
- In step 1's first session the probe's mode A moved issue.neighbors (+5.05%) and host_finish (+5.31%) at 12,288
atoms, and host_finish (+2.49%) at 98,304 atoms in float64, beyond the tolerance of 2%. That result stands as a
failed check: its split is not used.
- The session cannot say why, for a reason that rests on the base alone: the alternation put the bases at the ends
of every round (positions 1 and 4) and the probe's modes in the middle (2 and 3). The build is thus confounded
with the position, and the spread of base against base again compares end positions only. Position matters: in
the bench loop the first run of every round, always a base, took 2.62-2.72 ms at 12,288 atoms against
2.48-2.56 for every other run.
## The session from now on
- **Five settings:** base; the probe build with `OMNIMD_HOST_PROBE` unset (**mode 0**: the marks compiled in and
never taken, the allocator wrapper present and not timing); mode A; mode B; base again.
- **Order:** a Williams design of 10 rounds (two Latin squares, the second the mirror of the first), so that each
setting takes each position twice and follows each other setting twice. Rows, by setting in the order above:
- **A discarded run** at the head of every case in every round, after the card check: the first setting of that
row, run once and set aside.
- **Cases:** water 12,288 and 98,304 atoms, float32 with tables. The new session's result replaces the first
session's for both. The float64 case is not repeated: no clause of steps 1b and 2 reads its split (float64 is a
control, and the bars are taken in float32), so its first result stands as recorded.
- Unchanged: held to the P-cores and the mask checked, the card checked free before and after every round (a round
that ends on a busy card is set aside and run again), K = 100 at 12,288 atoms and 20 at 98,304, the check of the
rule as written (medians over rounds of the stage means, tolerance max(spread, 2%), the spread of base against
base again).
## Outcomes, written before the run (the session runs once and its result stands)
Mode A is held to the check, as the rule says; mode 0 is held to the same check to say why if A fails. "Passes"
means each of host_prepare, issue.neighbors and host_finish within the tolerance, at the case in question.
| Mode A | Mode 0 | Then |
| passes | either | The split of that case is used (mode A for the parts, mode B for the (a) projection and for (b)'s scatter). A failure of mode 0 alone is recorded. |
| fails | passes | The marks or the allocator's timing cost more than counted. Find the cost, revise the probe, and run one more session under this amendment. |
| fails | fails | The build itself moves the stages, and no thinner probe would pass. A decision of the rule is needed; no further run until it is made. |
## Two figures fixed now
- **The step 1 time of a loop** (the floor of step 1b, the projections of (d), (b) and the overlaps): mode A, the
profile phase, the median over the evaluations of a run, then the median over the session's rounds, at the
size in question.
- **The floor:** a loop whose step 1 time at 12,288 atoms is below 20.0 µs by that figure stays serial and projects
zero; at 20.0 µs or more it is above the floor. (The sort of the first session sat at 19.6-20.0 µs, inside the
shift in dispute, so only the new session decides it.)
# PR D rule, amendment 2: the session of step 1b
Written 2026-11-26 05:16 (UTC-6), after step 1 (`split-2.json`, notes in `split-2-notes.md`) and the advisor's
review of it. Nothing of step 1b had been built or run. This file's creation time is the time of the amendment.
It fixes what `rule-pr-d.txt` leaves open about step 1b: the settings, the order, the serial reference, the spin
window, the chunks, what is charged to (b), the guard of the results, and how the figures are read. Nothing else
changes.
(The draft on clause 3 of the A/B, called amendment 2 until now, becomes amendment 3. It is still a draft.)
## Why
- Step 1's mode A costs about 4 to 5 µs a part at 12,288 atoms against mode 0, the same binary with the probe off
(`split-2-notes.md`). So step 1's times carry the probe's own cost, and a saving taken as a step 1 time less a
step 1b time would mix two builds and two sessions.
- Split-1 showed that a plain alternation confounds the setting with its position in the round.
## The build
One probe build: step 1's probe (`tools/prd/probe_split.py`) plus the pool and the threaded loops
(`tools/prd/pool.rs`). It runs in mode B, so every pass writes into the evaluations the bench keeps. The setting is
chosen by `OMNIMD_POOL_K`.
## The four settings
- **s1, the serial loops** (`OMNIMD_POOL_K=1`; no pool is made):
- `fill`: the unchanged loop;
- the mapping of the species: the serial loop, writing into a buffer of types that the potential keeps (this is
(d)'s item 2);
- the scatter: the serial loop, writing into the kept evaluations (as mode B does);
- the sort: unchanged.
- **s2, s4 and s7: the threaded loops on k = 2, 4 and 7 parts** (`OMNIMD_POOL_K=k`): a pool of k - 1 workers, made
before the first evaluation.
- The mapping goes into the same kept buffer.
- `fill` and the mapping are threaded as described below.
- The scatter becomes a gather into the kept evaluations, in frame order, from the inverse of the sort's
permutation. The sort writes that inverse.
## The pool
- The pool is `tools/prd/pool.rs`:
- k - 1 workers, made once;
- the calling thread runs a share of each dispatch;
- a dispatch returns, or unwinds, only after every part has finished.
- Its unsafe core and its tests of the panic paths are reviewed before the session.
- **Spin window: 20 µs**, fixed now and the same for every setting and size.
- A worker that has finished a part keeps checking for the next dispatch for 20 µs of wall time, then parks.
- The window bridges `fill`'s two dispatches, which come back to back.
- It is too short to bridge any other gap of an evaluation (at least about 50 µs at 12,288 atoms), so it adds at
most about 3 × 20 µs of spinning on k - 1 threads per evaluation.
- It is not measured against other values.
## The chunks, and the order of each loop
Every threaded loop keeps the serial loop's order, so the device sees the same input to the bit.
- **Chunks:** each loop splits its work into 4k chunks of nearly equal length, in order. Any part, the caller
included, takes the next untaken chunk from a counter inside the job. So a part on an efficiency core, or one
sharing a core, takes fewer chunks instead of setting the dispatch's time.
- **The mapping:**
- Each chunk of the species maps into the same chunk of the kept buffer.
- On an error, the dispatch reports the atom of lowest index, with the serial loop's message.
- **`fill`, for each system of the pass:**
- **Pass 1, over chunks of the system's atoms:** the serial loop's first pass, plus the system's entry of each
atom (moved here from pass 2, with the same value). Each chunk also keeps a count of each cell, a largest
magnitude, and its atoms grouped by the range of cells they fall in, keeping their order.
- **Between the passes:** the caller writes the system's header from the largest magnitude over the chunks.
- **Pass 2, over 4k ranges of cells:** each range takes its cells' first entries from the counts of all chunks.
It then places the atoms of its cells, chunk by chunk in chunk order. So within a cell the atoms keep the
serial loop's order.
- A system whose atoms are not one contiguous range is packed by the serial loop. The session's frames are
single systems.
- **The scatter:** chunks of each evaluation's forces, in frame order. Each chunk is gathered from the device's
results through the inverse permutation.
## What is charged to (b)
- Each loop's interval of the probe holds its dispatches and the caller's work between them: `fill`'s header and
the reading of the counts.
- The sort's interval holds the writing of the inverse. Its rise over s1 is charged to the scatter.
- Scratch is kept across evaluations. The probe's count of allocations in each interval must not rise against s1
in any interval; the summary reports it.
## Sizes and phases
- Water, float32 with tables (`--compress 0.5`), at 1,536, 3,072, 6,144, 12,288 and 98,304 atoms.
- The 3,072- and 6,144-atom frames are `run/prd/frames`.
- The others are `mlmd/bench/cases`.
- `--bench K --profile` with K = 400, 300, 200, 100 and 20 respectively.
- Every figure comes from the profile phase. For each run, take the median over its evaluations; then take the
median over the rounds.
## Order
- **The square:** a Williams square of the four settings, by index s1, s2, s4, s7 = 0, 1, 2, 3. Its rows are 0132,
1203, 2310 and 3021. The session runs it twice, for 8 rounds. Each setting then takes each position twice and
follows each other setting twice.
- **Each round:**
- The card is checked free first.
- For each size in ascending order: one discarded run of the row's first setting, then the row's four settings.
- The card is checked again when the round ends. A round that ends on a busy card is set aside and run again, at
most 4 attempts.
- **Two sessions, each its own 8 rounds:**
1. held to the P-cores (`affine.py 0xFFFC`; the runner checks mask 0xfffc);
2. then unmasked (the runner checks that its mask is the system's).
## The guard, in every run
- **When:** the bench's first evaluation, outside both timed phases.
- **What it does:** it runs both paths of each loop on the same input and compares them to the bit:
- the threaded mapping against the serial one;
- the threaded `fill`'s words against the serial `fill`'s;
- the threaded scatter against the serial scatter. The threaded scatter writes into evaluations first filled with
NaN, so that a value left unwritten shows.
- **On a difference:** the run stops with an error, and the session stops. A loop that is wrong has no time worth
reading.
- **The results check:** as in step 1, each run's first evaluation is compared with s1's first run of its size.
Energies must be identical to the bit; the differences of forces and virials are recorded.
## How the figures are read (written before the run; the session's result stands)
1. **Saving of a loop on k parts:** its time in s1 minus its time in sk, both from the same session.
- This is how this amendment reads the rule's "its step 1 time minus its step 1b time on k threads".
- For the scatter, subtract also the sort's rise in sk over s1.
2. **The serial check:** s1's medians on the P-cores, at 12,288 and 98,304 atoms, against split-2's:
- `fill` against mode A's `fill` (124.02 and 1,039.12 µs);
- the scatter against mode B's (70.40 and 576.16 µs);
- the mapping against mode A's `map_types` less its allocations (27.68 - 3.50 = 24.18 and 227.49 - 18.97 =
Each must be within max(10%, 3 µs). If one is not, that loop's projection is not used until the cause is found
and recorded. A change to the probe means another session under this amendment.
3. **c:** take the unmasked session at 12,288 atoms, and the total of the mapping, `fill` and the scatter with the
sort's rise. c is the k of 2, 4 and 7 with the least total. If two are within 5% of each other, the smaller
wins.
4. **T:** take the unmasked session with k = c. T is the least size at which, at that size and every larger one,
the total on k parts is at least 10% less than s1's. T is at most 12,288. If no size up to 12,288 qualifies, the

## What the stamped rule says
A/B clause 3: "Energies, forces and virials are identical to the base's to the bit, at 88, 12,288 and 98,304 atoms,
in float32 and float64. (a), (d) and (b) reorder no sum, so this is the right bar for them. (c) is held to it as
well, since the order of atoms in each cell must stay the same."
## Why it cannot hold as written
- The force kernels add each center's own sum (`mlmd/native/src/gpu_model.rs` line 376 at af9ff5a) and its
neighbors' forces (lines 556, 665 and 1199) with `atomicAdd` on doubles, in no fixed order. The record says so
already: on the 83 HAP frames of the sealed test, two runs of one build differ by up to 9e-15 eV/Å
(`mlmd/bench/results/SUMMARY.md` line 546).
- Where a force kernel's block does not form its sums across its warps in a fixed order, each warp's sums are added
into the block's total with `atomicAdd` (lines 366-373), so a center's virial can move in its last bits too. That
is the case at 12,288 and 98,304 atoms in both precisions, and not at 88 (`force_sums` false and true in
`mlmd/bench/results/force-exact-lanes-rtx4090-2026-11-23.json`, for a08daf6, whose evaluation force kernels af9ff5a
keeps). The frame's sums then add the atoms' energies and virials in a fixed order: on the device from 576
centers (the comment at lines 1282-1300), and below that on the host in the kernel's order (`frame_sums_on_host`,
line 2631). So the energies do not move.
- The records show both (`rule-pr-d-amend-5-evidence-2.txt`, which replaces `rule-pr-d-amend-5-evidence.txt`: that
file left out step 1's first session in float32):
- In every compared run of step 1, of the base and of the probe build, the energies were the first base run's to
the bit. In step 1b, which ran its probe build alone, every run had the energies of the first run of its size.
- In step 1 forces differed by up to 11 units in the last place of a double (ulp) of the largest |force| (split-1
line 150: float32, 98,304 atoms), and virials by up to 2 ulp of the largest |virial|.
- The base build alone, 20 runs in each of the six cases of the clause (`base-spread-1.json`): the energies the
same in every run, every value finite, forces differing by up to 9.75 ulp (88 atoms, float32) and virials by up
to 1 ulp (none at 88 atoms).
- So the base fails the stamped clause against itself, and a candidate that changed nothing would fail it too.
## What a bar on the results alone cannot see
- **A value left unwritten.** (a) writes into evaluations the caller keeps. A force it failed to write would keep
the last pass's value, and the A/B evaluates one frame over and over, so the stale value would agree with the
base. The first evaluation, the one the bench prints, is made before anything is reused.
- **A last-bit change in the device's input.** A position wrapped or rounded otherwise (another order of operations,
a fused multiply-add) moves the results by about as much as the atomics do, and passes any bar that they pass.
- The order of the atoms within a cell is not among these. If a loop placed the atoms of a cell in another order,
the search would still give the same neighbor list, bit for bit. It ranks each center's candidates by distance,
atom and delta and fills the slots from those ranks alone (`mlmd/gpu/src/nlist.rs`: the key `before` at lines
30-35, the ties at 174-192, the ranks and slots at 419-445). Its serial fallback, `serial_center` (lines 88-172),
inserts by the same key. The results would move no more than the atomics move them between any two runs. The
stamped clause's reason for holding (c) to that order was wrong.
## Clause 3, as amended
1. **Energies** identical to the base's to the bit.
2. **Forces and virials** within 64 ulp of a double: the largest absolute difference of each kind is at most 64 times
`math.ulp` of the largest absolute value of that kind in the first base run's evaluation, in float32 as in float64
(the evaluations hold doubles in both). A value that is not finite, or a difference that is not a number, fails;
a largest difference that skips NaN does not count.
- Over step 1 and the base alone, in all six cases, the base against itself came to at most 11 ulp for forces and
2 for virials (`rule-pr-d-amend-5-evidence-2.txt`), so the bar leaves a margin of more than five times for
forces and thirty for virials. The 64 is the early draft's, set before any of these runs, and left as it was once
the six cases were measured. The base alone was first run twice a case to try the runner; that smoke is kept as
`base-spread-smoke.json` and `.txt` (at most 9 ulp and 1).
- The base again is held to the same bar. If it fails, nothing passes, and the cause is looked into.
3. **Where, and what is compared.** Items 1 and 2 are judged in a functional session of their own beside the timed
A/B, run as `base-spread-1` was: the base, the change and the base again, 5 rounds, one process a run, the card
checked free before each case. The cases are those of the stamped clause, each on the bench's plain path (one
frame, no `--bench-batches`) with `--bench 1` and tables from 0.5 Å: 88 atoms, the small set's HAP frame
(`mlmd/bench/cases/hap/hap_bulk__H4Ca20O52P12.frame.jsonl` with the committee's first model,
`hap-iter0-pre/ens4-f32-0.native.json`), and water at 12,288 and 98,304 atoms (`water-se_e2_a-float64.native.json`),
each in float32 and float64. In each case, each run's first evaluation (made before the bench reuses anything,
and printed as now) is held against the first base run of the session; from (a) on, each run's check pass (item
4) against that run's own first evaluation. The timed A/B's runs are held to the same items wherever they print
the same lines.
4. **(a): every value written.** (a) writes into kept evaluations for one frame and one model (`eval_into`): the MD
loop of one system and the bench's plain path take it. The barostat's trial evaluation and `MlipReplicas`'
batches keep `eval` and `eval_batch`.
- **The bench's check pass.** (a)'s PR adds it to the bench, after the timed and profile loops and outside the
timed interval: every value of the kept evaluation set to NaN, one more pass written into it by the same method
as the timed loop, an assertion that it wrote in place (the forces' address is kept), `validate` on what it
wrote, and a line on stderr with what the runner holds to items 1 and 2: whether the energy's bits are the
first evaluation's, the largest differences of forces and virials from it (a NaN counted as infinite), and
whether every value is finite. It runs wherever the timed loop wrote into a kept evaluation, without a flag
(the base's bench refuses flags it does not know: the last arm of its match of flags), and stays in the bench,
so it runs in the A/B of every later PR.
- **A suite test** on the device, run with `OMNIMD_REQUIRE_GPU=1` so that it cannot skip, in float32 and float64:
frames evaluated one after the other into the same kept evaluation, every value set to NaN before each; two
frames of one atom count whose species differ at some index (the second asserted written in place), and one of
another count (the forces grow or shrink). Each is held by items 1 and 2 against a fresh evaluation of its
frame, made by a potential that has seen no other frame; that evaluation also gives item 2's scale. First, two
such fresh evaluations of each frame are seen to agree within item 2's bar.
- **A test of the engine's path:** a few steps of the MD loop through the engine's `Backend` (`main.rs`'s own
test module), with a potential that writes in place: a test double in the box of `Backend::NativeGpu`, or the
device's potential. The test asserts that the potential's `eval_into` is the method called. The MD loop writes
into a spare evaluation and swaps it in at commit, so the committed forces alternate between two buffers. The
test therefore also asserts that the committed forces' address at each step from the third on is the one of
two steps before, and differs from the one of the step before. The default cannot give that. It assigns a
fresh evaluation while the buffer of two steps before is still held, so the new forces get another address.
